title: Questions to ask the interviewer
examples: What does a typical day look like in this role?
How is success measured for someone in this position?
Could you describe the team I would be working with?

explain.say: When you interview, asking about the role helps you understand the day to day work.
Next, ask about the team structure to see who you will collaborate with.
It is also important to ask how success is actually measured in this job.
For example, you could ask, what are the key performance indicators for this position?
A common mistake is asking questions you could easily find online.

faq.q: Should I ask about company culture?
faq.a: Yes, it is a good general question. You could also ask about work-life balance or team communication styles. You might ask, what is the general vibe here? Or, how do people usually interact?

faq.q: Is it okay to ask about training?
faq.a: Absolutely, this shows you are committed to learning. You can ask about onboarding processes or professional development budgets. You could ask, what support do new hires receive?

faq.q: When should I ask about salary?
faq.a: It is usually best to wait until the interviewer brings it up or until the final stages. You can phrase it as, what is the compensation structure for this role? You might ask, what is the salary band?

faq.q: What if I don't know the industry well?
faq.a: It is fine to admit you are learning, but always follow up with questions showing you are researching. You could ask, what are the biggest industry trends right now? You might ask, what keeps you busy in this field?

faq.q: Should I prepare questions for the hiring manager?
faq.a: Yes, always prepare thoughtful questions. This shows genuine interest and preparation. You could ask, what does success look like in the first six months?

facts: Asking about the role shows your interest in the actual tasks.
Questions about the team show you care about collaboration.
Understanding success measures helps you know what to achieve.
Good questions demonstrate preparation and engagement.

quiz.say: If you want to know the specific goals for the job, which area should you focus on?
quiz.why: KPIs directly tell you what measurable results the company expects.

wrong.1: This focuses on people, not measurable results.
wrong.2: This describes how you work, not how well you must perform.
wrong.3: This is general knowledge, not related to your performance goals.

quiz.say: Which question best shows you understand the day-to-day work?

options.show: What does a typical week involve?
options.say: What does a typical week involve?

options.show: What is the budget for this department?
options.say: What is the budget for this department?

quiz.why: This question asks for a routine description, which defines the role.

wrong.1: This is too broad and general for the role itself.
wrong.2: This is about hierarchy, not the tasks performed.
wrong.3: This is a financial question, not a task description.

quiz.say: If you want to know about collaboration, which topic is best to question?

options.show: What are the department's long-term goals?
options.say: What are the department's long-term goals?

options.show: What is the company's biggest product?
options.say: What is the company's biggest product?

quiz.why: Communication methods reveal the nature of teamwork and interaction.

wrong.0: This is too high-level; the team question should be more specific.
wrong.1: This is purely financial data and not related to teamwork.
wrong.3: This is about the company's output, not the team's process.
